A write-ahead log is a file that contains a record of all changes made to the database. When a change is made to the database, the change is first written to the log, and then the change is written to the database itself. This ensures that the log always contains a complete and consistent record of all changes made to the database, even if the database itself is corrupted or lost.
When a database crashes, the log can be used to recover the database to a consistent state. The database can be restored to a point in time just before the crash by replaying all the changes recorded in the log up to that point. This ensures that the database is consistent and up-to-date, even if some changes were not written to the database before the crash.
The log can also be used to recover from a situation where the database is inconsistent, such as when a transaction is rolled back. In this case, the log can be used to undo the changes made by the transaction, restoring the database to a consistent state.
